clue.text: Lexicographer wanting son to become artist

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word for son is taken away from the lexicographer's name

parts.note: Dr Samuel Johnson compiled the famous 1755 English dictionary
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dictionary-maker gives up on his boy, who would rather paint.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking SON from JOHNSON leaves the painter's surname; Augustus John was a celebrated Welsh artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus John was a famous Welsh portrait painter, so the name stands for an artist.

clue.text: Judge ordered steak with cold potato skins

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A judge orders steak and cold baked potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Potatoes baked in their jackets have these as their skins.

clue.text: Herod massacred large number

indicators.note: massacred means the letters are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: King Herod's massacre of the innocents killed many.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a crowd or great mass of people.

clue.text: Strain and stiffness of neck when head is displaced

indicators.note: displaced here means knocked out of the word altogether, so that letter is lost

parts.note: a crick is a painful stiffness in the neck
the head of the neck-stiffness word is its first letter, C

explanation.surface: A pulled muscle and a stiff neck after jerking the head out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when head is displaced' says CRICK loses its head, the first letter C; 'displaced' means knocked out, not moved elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrench or sprain a joint is to strain it; the word is a variant of wrick.

clue.text: Child's into Fantasia? Not half, not half!.

indicators.note: not half means only half of each word is kept, its first part
the repeated not half confirms that both words are cut to their first halves

explanation.surface: A child is really into the Disney film Fantasia; not half!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here each 'not half' halves a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby or very young child is an infant.

clue.text: Know about family heading New York's Irish community

indicators.note: heading means the first piece comes ahead of the New York abbreviation
about means the word for know goes around the family word

parts.note: ken means knowledge or to know
ilk means type or family
NY is the abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: Knowledge about a family leading New York's Irish community.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilkenny is an Irish county and city, so it is an Irish community.

clue.text: Article holding extra in return?

indicators.note: holding means the article contains the next piece within it

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in return means the word for extra is read backwards

parts.note: odd can mean extra, as in the odd one over

explanation.surface: A shop item comes with a bonus thrown in on returning it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' turns ODD into DDO, which AN then holds. The whole clue also describes the answer: something extra attached.
explanation.definitionFit: An optional supplementary item is something extra attached to a main purchase.

clue.text: Fool injecting fix with drug takers — they're only interested in quick profit

definitions.text: they're only interested in quick profit

indicators.note: injecting here means the fool takes the fix into itself, so it surrounds it

parts.note: an ass is a fool
set means fix
trippers are people taking hallucinogenic drugs

explanation.surface: A fool shooting up with drug users; they only care about fast money.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporate raiders buy firms to sell off their parts for fast gain.

clue.text: The German painter's an expert on greens?

parts.note: die is the German feminine for the
Titian was the Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: The German painter is an expert on vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrition specialist advises on eating vegetables, the greens of the question.

clue.text: See about daughter after weight goes up in conspicuous way

indicators.note: after means the see with daughter follows the weight
goes up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a ton is a weight

indicators.note: about means the see is placed around the daughter

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Look at the daughter after her weight increases.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something remarkably or eminently is acting in a conspicuous manner.

clue.text: I play big choral composition — as The Childhood of Christ might be described

definitions.text: as The Childhood of Christ might be described

indicators.note: composition means the letters are composed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: I perform a large choral work like Berlioz's oratorio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' looks like the musical work but is the anagram signal. Berlioz's L'Enfance du Christ tells the story of Christ's early life.
explanation.definitionFit: A work recounting the early life story of a person is described as telling that life.

clue.text: City Road has one in informal coffee house

indicators.note: in places road and one inside the cafe word

parts.note: caff is British slang for a cheap cafe
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A street has a greasy spoon on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh capital is a city.

clue.text: Hustles corruptly, being extremely rich

indicators.note: corruptly means the letters are corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hustles dishonestly and becomes very wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush means lavish or richly abundant, so the superlative is extremely rich.

clue.text: Medical crisis is curtailed by drug coming to light

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an emergency is an urgent medical crisis
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A health emergency is cut short by a new medicine coming to light.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerging into view is the process of coming to light.

clue.text: Position for bronze heads of two horses in Rodin's design

indicators.note: heads of means taking the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A bronze sculpture by Rodin shows two horses' heads.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bronze' of the surface is the sculptor's metal, but in the definition it is the medal for coming in after gold and silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronze medal is awarded for finishing in that place, behind first and second.

clue.text: Walk casually, for example, around tree

indicators.note: around means the first word wraps around the tree

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example
an ash is a tree

explanation.surface: Stroll idly, perhaps around a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk in a showy, swaying, unhurried manner is a synonym for strolling casually.

clue.text: Informed after adding recapitulation

indicators.note: after means the word for informed comes after the adding word

parts.note: summing means adding up
up means informed, as in up on the news

explanation.surface: A knowledgeable person totting up figures for a review.
explanation.definitionFit: A final summary that restates the main points is a recapitulation.

clue.text: Contemptuously putting out Stilton with last of Derby

indicators.note: putting out means putting the letters out of place, rearranging them
last of means take the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone sneeringly serves Stilton alongside the remains of a Derby cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is also an English cheese, which fits the cheeseboard picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting snootily, with a superior sneer, is behaving contemptuously.

clue.text: Damaged fin on fire during plane trip

indicators.note: damaged means the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: to light is to set fire to

explanation.surface: A plane's fin catches fire mid-flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something served aboard an aircraft while flying happens during the journey.

clue.text: Say. Brahms' fifth, turning out a fake?

definitions.text: Say. Brahms' fifth, turning out a fake?

indicators.note: turning out means expelling, so the letter a is thrown out of say
fifth picks the fifth letter of the composer's name

parts.note: phony means fake

explanation.surface: Is a supposed fifth by Brahms a forgery?
explanation.walkthrough: Brahms wrote only four symphonies, so a 'fifth' would indeed be fake, which makes the whole clue the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahms composed orchestral works of this kind; a fifth one would be a fake orchestral work.

clue.text: Virtuous — isn't commonly caught in showing hypocrisy

indicators.note: caught in means the colloquial word is held within the other

parts.note: sly means sneaky and two-faced
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: The goody-goody is, as people say, caught being a hypocrite.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy and good, like a canonised person, means virtuous.

clue.text: Meal's inside, following onset of downpour

indicators.note: following means the word for inside comes after the first piece
onset of means the start, the first letter of downpour

parts.note: inner means inside

explanation.surface: We eat indoors once the rain starts.
explanation.definitionFit: The main meal of the day is a familiar synonym for a meal.

clue.text: Source of valuable stone put in list

indicators.note: in means the word for put goes inside the list

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
set means put

explanation.surface: Where a precious gem came from is put on the inventory.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rosetta Stone, key to Egyptian hieroglyphs, is named after the town where it was found.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian town gave its name to the hieroglyph-deciphering stone found there.

clue.text: Pin as bishop moves, covering queen

indicators.note: covering in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a chess bishop moves diagonally, that is skew
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for queen

explanation.surface: A chess pin as the bishop moves to cover the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess a skewer is an attack on a piece with another behind it, adding to the chess picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A long thin spike for holding meat is a kind of pin.

clue.text: Reptilia cast part of lower body

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A reptile's shed skin forms part of the lower body.
explanation.definitionFit: The ilium is the hip bone, so the adjective refers to the lower body region.

clue.text: They're such as Coleridge — Keats and Poe left out?

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Coleridge's crowd excludes Keats and Poe.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge, Wordsworth and Southey were the poets of the English Lake District group.

clue.text: Magistrate raising lash hardheartedly

indicators.note: raising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards
heartedly puts the hard letter at the heart of lash

parts.note: a rope's end is used to lash
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An official heartlessly raises the whip.
explanation.definitionFit: The ephors were the five annually elected magistrates of ancient Sparta.

clue.text: Passively accompany nameless Filipino

indicators.note: nameless means without n, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: to tag along is to follow along passively

explanation.surface: An unnamed person from the Philippines just follows along.
explanation.definitionFit: The national language of the Philippines is a Filipino tongue.

clue.text: Plant strike vindicating labour

parts.note: wort is an old word for a plant, as in St John's wort
hit means strike

explanation.surface: A factory strike justifies the workers' effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying an effort paid off is idiomatic for justifying the work put in.

clue.text: City worker raised capital in Pounds to be invested in Yens

indicators.note: to be invested in means these pieces are placed inside the yens

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for yen, so two yens give two Ys
up means raised

indicators.note: capital means the initial letter of pounds

explanation.surface: A financier raises capital in sterling to put into yen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' is the City of London, the financial district, and its young professionals were the 1980s yuppies.
explanation.definitionFit: A young urban professional typically worked in finance in the City of London.

clue.text: Sweet and sour?

definitions.meaning: a pastry with fruit or jam filling served as a sweet course

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a pastry dessert and an adjective meaning acid-tasting.

clue.text: A quantity of paper almost one metre square, perhaps

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: a ream is 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: A stack of paper nearly a metre square.
explanation.definitionFit: A square metre is a unit for measuring surface extent.
